what_it_does: Quantum computers can tackle certain problems far faster than classical chips, but today they operate as separate, loosely connected devices: a classical host computer sends a job to the quantum processor, waits for results, adjusts parameters, and repeats — with each round-trip taking milliseconds. Many promising quantum algorithms require real-time classical feedback after every quantum step, so this lag is a hard bottleneck. Qtenon is a custom chip (built using RISC-V, a popular open processor design, extended with new instructions for quantum work) that sits directly alongside the quantum processor and communicates through a shared memory region, cutting round-trip delays to nanoseconds. It includes a dedicated control pipeline for issuing quantum operations and novel instructions that let software coordinate quantum and classical steps with fine-grained timing.
